records.quote: We have studied hydrostatic pressure dependence of the electronic, optical, thermodynamic and thermoelectric properties of CsVO3 via first principles calculations.
context_quotes: The semi-classic Boltzmann transport theory was used to explore pressure and temperature dependencies of the thermoelectric properties.

records.subject: Quasi-harmonic Debye model
records.object: Pressure and temperature dependencies of CsVO3 isochore and isobar heat capacities, lattice thermal conductivity, volume thermal expansion coefficient and Debye temperature
records.conditions: First-principles study.
records.quote: We have studied hydrostatic pressure dependence of the electronic, optical, thermodynamic and thermoelectric properties of CsVO3 via first principles calculations.
context_quotes: Pressure and temperature dependencies of the thermal parameters, viz., isochore and isobar heat capacities, lattice thermal conductivity, volume thermal expansion coefficient and Debye temperature, were explored through the quasi-harmonic Debye model.
modality_evidence: We have studied hydrostatic pressure dependence of the electronic, optical, thermodynamic and thermoelectric properties of CsVO3 via first principles calculations.

Pressure and temperature dependencies of the thermal parameters, viz., isochore and isobar heat capacities, lattice thermal conductivity, volume thermal expansion coefficient and Debye temperature, were explored through the quasi-harmonic Debye model.

paper.note: Temperature and pressure dependencies described only as investigated or explored are not treated as findings.

change_log.reason: Bind both parameter sets to CsVO3.

conditions.after: CsVO3; comparison with available experimental counterparts.

change_log.reason: Retain the bandgap calculation's potential qualifier.

before: It is found that the bandgap increases with increasing pressure.
after: Analysis of the energy band dispersion calculated within the TB-mBJ potential reveals that CsVO3 is a direct bandgap semiconductor with a fundamental bandgap of 3.14 eV.
It is found that the bandgap increases with increasing pressure.

conditions.after: First-principles calculations; energy-band dispersion within the TB-mBJ potential.

change_log.reason: Bind the optical quantities to CsVO3.

after: Frequency-dependent linear macroscopic optical coefficients, namely absorption coefficient, refractive index, extinction coefficient, reflectivity and optical conductivity, were deduced from the calculated real and imaginary parts of the complex dielectric function under hydrostatic pressure effect.
